encounters.cc: Fatigue, mild jaundice, and dark urine for 2 weeks

lines: Fatigue, mild jaundice, and dark urine for 2 weeks
He presents to the clinic with a 2-week history of fatigue, mild jaundice, and dark urine.
He denies any significant medical history and has not traveled outside the country recently.
He reports having had multiple sexual partners in the past year and occasionally using intravenous drugs.
On physical examination, he is afebrile, with scleral icterus and mild hepatomegaly.
No ascites or spider angiomas are noted.
- IgM hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc IgM): Negative
- IgG hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc IgG): Positive

encounters.cc: Routine follow-up for HIV with intermittent fever, oral thrush, and 10-lb weight loss over 3 months

lines: Routine follow-up for HIV with intermittent fever, oral thrush, and 10-lb weight loss over 3 months
He returns for HIV follow-up following his January 2020 hepatitis evaluation.
He has not yet started antiretroviral therapy and reports intermittent fever, oral thrush, and a 10-lb unintentional weight loss over the past 3 months.
He has no documented history of measles, mumps, or rubella infection, and his vaccination records are unavailable.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Currently unemployed.
Physical examination reveals white plaques on the lateral tongue that cannot be scraped off.
Laboratory studies show a CD4+ T-cell count of 100 cells/mm³.
The clinician considers administering the MMR vaccine as part of routine preventive care.

encounters.cc: Multiple small flesh-colored bumps on lower abdomen for 3 months

lines: Multiple small flesh-colored bumps on lower abdomen for 3 months
The patient with HIV, chronic hepatitis B and C, and opioid use disorder (intravenous) presents for evaluation with a 3-month history of multiple, small, flesh-colored bumps on his lower abdomen.
He reports the lesions are asymptomatic but slowly increasing in number, and he inquires about treatment options for these lesions.
He is sexually active with multiple partners and uses condoms inconsistently.
On physical examination, you note 10-15 dome-shaped papules, each approximately 2-5 mm in diameter, with a characteristic central umbilication.
No lymphadenopathy or other skin lesions are noted.

encounters.cc: Widespread skin lesions on trunk, face, and upper extremities for 6 months

lines: Widespread skin lesions on trunk, face, and upper extremities for 6 months
The patient, with HIV and chronic hepatitis, returns to Dermatology six months after prior abdominal lesions.
He reports that the lesions began as small, painless bumps on his trunk but have since spread to his upper extremities and face.
He denies any pruritus or discomfort associated with the lesions.
His past medical history is significant for intravenous drug use.
He has been sexually active with multiple partners, without consistent use of protection
His temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg, and heart rate is 88 beats per minute.
On physical examination, you note multiple firm, flesh-colored, dome-shaped papules with central umbilication on his trunk, arms, and face.
The patient appears thin and has oral thrush.

encounters.cc: Increasing facial puffiness and leg swelling over the past 3 weeks

lines: Increasing facial puffiness and leg swelling over the past 3 weeks
The patient is a 34-year-old male with human immunodeficiency virus infection, chronic hepatitis B and C, and history of opportunistic infections including molluscum contagiosum and oral thrush.
He presents with increasing facial puffiness and leg swelling over the past 3 weeks.
Physical exam shows periorbital and peripheral edema. There is an abdominal fluid wave.
Laboratory studies show low serum albumin and elevated cholesterol.
There is a "spike and dome" appearance of the glomeruli on silver stain.
Immunofluorescence shows subepithelial deposition of IgG and complement protein C3.

encounters.cc: Fever, malaise, and right-sided lower abdominal pain radiating to the groin for 2 weeks

lines: Fever, malaise, and right-sided lower abdominal pain radiating to the groin for 2 weeks

Patient with HIV, chronic hepatitis B/C, and IV opioid use disorder, recently seen for swelling, presents to the emergency department with a 2-week history of fever, malaise, and right-sided lower abdominal pain radiating to his groin.
He denies any trauma or recent travel.
With a history of intravenous drug use
On examination, his temperature is 38.5°C, heart rate is 100 bpm, and blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg.
Abdominal examination reveals tenderness in the right lower quadrant with no rebound or guarding.
Hip extension on the right side elicits severe pain.
A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast is performed, which shows a 4 cm abscess within the right psoas muscle.

encounters.cc: Fever, malaise, and new-onset lower back pain for 2 weeks

lines: Fever, malaise, and new-onset lower back pain for 2 weeks

The patient, a 35-year-old male with HIV, chronic hepatitis B and C, and prior psoas abscess, presents to the emergency department with a 2-week history of fever, malaise, and a new-onset lower back pain.
He denies any recent trauma or heavy lifting.
With a history of intravenous drug use
His temperature is 38.7°C, blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg, heart rate is 105 bpm, and respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute.
Physical examination reveals a grade III/VI systolic murmur best heard at the right sternal border, and there is tenderness over the lumbar spine.
There are track marks noted on his forearms.
- Urinalysis: No bacteria or white blood cells
A transthoracic echocardiogram shows vegetations on the tricuspid valve.

encounters.cc: Progressive weakness in legs and difficulty walking with tingling in feet for 1 week

lines: Progressive weakness in legs and difficulty walking with tingling in feet for 1 week

The patient is a 35-year-old male with HIV, chronic hepatitis B and C, opioid use disorder, and recent hospitalizations for infective endocarditis and psoas abscess, who presents with progressive weakness in his legs and difficulty walking for one week.
He also reports tingling sensations in his feet.
He has a past medical history of intravenous drug use and unprotected sexual encounters with multiple partners.
He has not been tested for HIV.
Vital signs are stable, and there are no signs of respiratory distress.
On examination, the patient has bilateral lower extremity weakness, areflexia, and decreased sensation in a glove-and-stocking distribution.
Initial laboratory tests are as follows:
- Complete blood count: within normal limits
- Comprehensive metabolic panel: within normal limits
Nerve conduction studies show slowed conduction velocities and prolonged distal latencies consistent with demyelination.
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis reveals an elevated protein level with a normal white blood cell count.
